questions.def: "Rose" is intransitive (no object). "Raised" requires an object.
questions.question: The price of oil ___ sharply yesterday.

questions.def: "Raised" is transitive (takes an object: prices).
questions.question: The company ___ its prices due to inflation.

questions.def: "Lay" is transitive (takes an object: book).
questions.question: Please ___ the book on the table.

questions.def: "Lay" (past tense of lie) is intransitive.
questions.question: He ___ down for a nap after lunch.

questions.def: "Lays" is transitive (takes an object: egg).
questions.question: The hen ___ an egg every morning.

questions.def: "Sit" is intransitive. "Set" needs an object.
questions.question: He ___ in his favorite armchair.

questions.def: "Set" is transitive and means to place something.
questions.question: Please ___ the vase on the mantelpiece carefully.

questions.def: "Sank" is the past tense of the intransitive verb sink.
questions.question: The sun ___ behind the clouds.

questions.def: "Hang" is intransitive here (to be suspended).
questions.question: The picture ___ on the wall.

questions.def: "Hanged" is used for execution (transitive).
questions.question: They ___ the prisoner this morning.

questions.def: "Flows" is intransitive. Requires no object.
questions.question: The river ___ to the sea.

questions.def: Floated is correct. It shows he put the boat in the water.
questions.question: He floated the boat down the river.

questions.def: "Wakes" is intransitive when meaning to stop sleeping.
questions.question: She ___ up early every morning.

questions.def: "Woke" is transitive (takes an object: baby).
questions.question: The loud noise ___ the baby.

questions.def: "Started" and "began" are intransitive in this context.
questions.question: The meeting ___ at 2 PM.

questions.def: Started is correct here, as it takes a direct object.
questions.question: He started the engine with little difficulty.

questions.def: "Grew" is intransitive when meaning to increase in size.
questions.question: The company ___ rapidly last year.

questions.def: "Grows" is transitive (takes an object: wheat).
questions.question: The farmer ___ wheat in his fields.

questions.def: "Swung" is the past tense of the intransitive verb swing.
questions.question: The door ___ open.

questions.def: "Swung" is the correct past tense when transitive.
questions.question: He swang the bat with all his might.

questions.def: "Rang" is intransitive (to make a ringing sound).
questions.question: The phone ___ loudly.

questions.def: "Rang" is transitive (takes an object: bell).
questions.question: He ___ the bell to summon the waiter.

questions.def: "Melted" is intransitive (to become liquid).
questions.question: The ice ___ in the sun.

questions.def: Melted is correct here as it takes a direct object.
questions.question: The heat melted the ice cream very quickly.

questions.def: "Fall" is intransitive. No object.
questions.question: The leaves ___ from the trees in autumn.

questions.def: "Felled" is transitive (takes an object: tree).
questions.question: The lumberjack ___ the tree with an axe.

questions.def: "Sank" is intransitive (went down).
questions.question: The ship ___ after hitting the iceberg.

questions.def: Intransitive 'rise' means to increase. 'Raise' needs a direct object.
questions.question: The price of oil ___ sharply after the announcement.

questions.def: Transitive 'raise' means to lift something. It requires a direct object.
questions.question: She ___ her hand to ask a question.

questions.def: 'Sit' (intransitive) means to be in a seated position. 'Set' is transitive.
questions.question: He ___ in the same chair every day.
